competition: Myanmar Open Mathematics Competition, Senior II (Mathematical Society of Myanmar)

problems.problem: Line up the numbers $1$ to $15$ such that if you add any two numbers that are next to each other, you get a square number.

When A3-size paper is folded once, we get two A4-size papers. A3-size paper and A4-size paper are similar rectangles.
(a) Find the exact value of the ratio of length and width of the A4-size paper.
(b) If the area of an A4-size paper is $625\ \text{cm}^2$, compute the length and width of the A4-size paper in cm correct to 1 decimal place.

A function $f$, defined for all positive numbers, satisfies the equation
$$2f(x)+f\left(\frac1x\right)=3x.$$
Find the function $f$.

Let $A(x_1,y_1)$ and $B(x_2,y_2)$ be two points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane. Show that
$$\left|\tan^{-1}\frac{y_2}{x_2}-\tan^{-1}\frac{y_1}{x_1}\right|=\cos^{-1}\frac{x_1x_2+y_1y_2}{\sqrt{x_1^2+y_1^2}\sqrt{x_2^2+y_2^2}}.$$
In $\triangle ABC$, $AB=8$, $BC=7\sqrt2$ and $CA=5\sqrt2$. Find the exact value of radius of the circumscribed circle of $\triangle ABC$.
In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A=90^\circ$. The angle bisector $CD$ of interior $\angle ACB$ meets segment $AB$ at $D$. If $AD=1$ and $DB=2$, find the length of $CD$ and degree measure of $\angle B$.

Sequence $u_1,u_2,u_3,\dots$ is defined by $u_1=1$, $u_2=3$, $u_{n+2}=3u_{n+1}-(u_1+u_2+\cdots+u_n)$ for $n\ge1$.
Prove, by induction, that $\dfrac{u_{n+1}}{u_n}>2$ for $n\ge1$.

In $\triangle ABC$, $AC>BC$ and the point $D$ lies on segment $AB$ such that $\angle ACD=\angle BCD$. The perpendicular bisector of segment $CD$ intersects the line $AB$ at $E$.
(a) Prove that $CE$ is tangent to the circumscribed circle of $\triangle ABC$.
(b) If $AB:BE=5:4$, find $AD:DB$.

Prove that, for positive numbers $x, y$ and $z$,
$$xy+yz+zx+\frac2x+\frac2y+\frac2z\ge9.$$

(a) Find the partial fractions of $\dfrac1{4r^2-1}$.
(a) Using Part (a), show that
$$\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac1{4r^2-1}=\frac n{2n+1}.$$
(b) Determine the value of
$$\frac1{1\times3}+\frac1{3\times5}+\frac1{5\times7}+\cdots+\frac1{99\times101}.$$
(c) Determine the value of
$$\frac1{1\times3}+\frac1{3\times5}+\frac1{5\times7}+\cdots.$$

Given a positive integer $m$, find the positive integers $n_1,n_2,\dots,n_k$ such that $n_1+n_2+\cdots+n_k=m$ and $n_1(m-n_1)+n_2(m-n_2)+\cdots+n_k(m-n_k)$ is maximum for all possible choice of $n_1,n_2,\dots,n_k$.

Let $S$ denote a set of $n$ elements. Let $\Gamma$ be a (Sperner) collection of subsets of $S$ such that no one contains another:
$$\Gamma=\{A_1,A_2,\dots,A_k\}\text{ where }A_i\subset S,\text{ and }A_i\not\subset A_j\text{ if }i\ne j.$$
Prove that for any Sperner collection $\Gamma$,
$$|\Gamma|\le {}^nC_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor},$$
where $|\Gamma|$ is the number of elements of $\Gamma$ and $\lfloor \frac n2\rfloor$ is the greatest integer less than or equal to $\frac n2$.
Determine the number of positive integers less than $9010$ which are divisible by neither $7$ nor $9$ nor $11$.

Let $A=\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$. Find all functions $f:A\to A$ such that
$$f(x)+f(y)=(x+y)f(x)f(y)$$
for all $x\in A$ and $y\in A$.
In $\triangle ABC$, altitudes $AD$ and $BE$ intersect at $H$. Line $AD$ meets the circumcircle of $ABC$ at $F$ and the circumcircle of $BHC$ again at $G$. Prove that line $BF\perp CG$.

If $a$, $b$ and $c$ are distinct positive numbers, prove that
$$\frac{(a^2-b^2)^3+(b^2-c^2)^3+(c^2-a^2)^3}{(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)}>24abc.$$

Solve the system of equations
$$x+y=1,$$
$$\frac{\sqrt x-1}{\sqrt y-1}+\frac{\sqrt x}{\sqrt y}+\frac{\sqrt x+1}{\sqrt y+1}=3.$$

For $p>1$, $q>1$, $r>1$ and $s>1$, show that
$$\frac{p^2}{q-1}+\frac{q^2}{r-1}+\frac{r^2}{s-1}+\frac{s^2}{p-1}\ge16.$$

Consider $n$-letter words in which each letter is either A or B, and no three consecutive letters are equal to each other. Let $a_n$ be the number of such $n$-letter words. Now we have number sequence
$$a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4,\dots.$$
(a) Write down the values of $a_1,a_2$ and $a_3$.
(b) Determine a recurrence relation of $a_n,a_{n-1}$ and $a_{n-3}$ for $n\ge4$.
(c) What is the number of such 10-letter words?

For each positive integer $n$, let $u_n$ be the number of quadruplets $(p,q,r,s)$ of non-negative integers such that
$$p+q+r+4s=n.$$
Find $u_{2024}-u_{2020}$.

Find the number of all integer pairs $(a,b)$ such that
$$\frac1a+\frac1b=\frac1{2024}.$$

Show that $\dfrac{g}{g+h}=\dfrac{d}{d+e}\cdot\dfrac{b}{a+b}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/mm_2024_d2_p11_fig.png

In the figure, two triangles are congruent. Find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $a$, $b$, $c$, and $d$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/mm_2024_d2_p12_fig.png

If $b$ is a real number satisfying
$$b+\frac1b=10,$$
compute the numerical value of
$$(\sqrt b-3)(\sqrt b-1)(\sqrt b+1)(\sqrt b+3).$$
Nyan Nyan wants to colour each cell of a $5\times5$ table either red or blue so that there are exactly $4$ blue cells in every row and every column. In how many ways can Nyan Nyan do this?
Let $ABCDEF$ be a regular hexagon with area $a$. If the area of triangle $ACE$ is $b$, find the ratio $b/a$.
Suppose that $x$ and $y$ are positive integers such that $2024x=y^2$. Find the minimum possible value of $x+y$.

Define a sequence $\{z_n\}$ of complex numbers by $z_1=1$ and $z_{n+1}=\overline{z_n}+1+ni$, for all integers $n\ge1$.
a) Find a relation between $z_{n+2}$ and $z_n$.
b) Determine the value of $z_{2025}$.

At the Interuniversal Mathematical Olympiad (IMO), six problems are asked each year. Two friends - Lin Lin and Kyi Kyi - are preparing for the IMO and have decided to solve the problem set from IMO 2024. They attempt all 6 problems, and each of them solves exactly four out of the six problems.
• Each problem has been solved by at least one of the two friends.
• There are exactly two common problems that have been solved by both friends.
Find the number of all possible ordered pairs $(A,B)$ such that $A$ is the set of problems solved by Lin Lin and $B$ is the set of problems solved by Kyi Kyi.

Let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $ABC$. A circle passing through $B$ and $C$ intersects the sides $AB$ and $AC$ at points $D$ and $E$, respectively. Show that $DE\perp AO$. (The circumcenter of a non-degenerate triangle is the center of the circle passing through the three vertices of that triangle.)
Find the largest integer $x$ such that $\dfrac{x^2+5x+2010}{x-2}$ is an integer.
A sequence $\{a_n\}$ is defined by $a_1=\frac52$, $a_{n+1}=\sqrt{2a_n+3}$ for all $n\ge1$. Prove that $2<a_n<3$ for all positive integers $n$.

A cycling park is made out of semicircular paths joining points $A$ to $B$ as shown below. Ni Ni wants to cycle from point $A$ to $B$ without making sharp turns or turning around. An example of a path that Ni Ni can take is shown below. Find the number of ways Ni Ni can complete her cycling track.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/mm_2025_d1_p10_fig.png

Let $ABC$ be a right triangle with $\angle B=90^\circ$ and $AB=BC=1$. Let $D$ be a point inside $ABC$ such that $DC=BC$ and $\angle DCB=30^\circ$. Find the circumradius of $ADC$. (The circumradius of a non-degenerate triangle is the radius of the circle passing through the three vertices of that triangle.)

Consider the set $S=\{1,2,\cdots,20\}$. A person chooses three integers $i,j,k$ from $S$ such that $i<j<k$ and $i,j,k$ forms a geometric sequence, in that order, with a rational number $r$ as its common ratio.
a) Show that, when $r$ is written in the simplest form, the denominator of $r$ must be at most $4$.
b) Show that there are exactly five possible values of $r$, and state those values.

a) Prove that $x^3+y^3\ge x^2y+xy^2$ for all positive real numbers $x$ and $y$.
b) Let $a,b,c$ be positive real numbers such that $abc=1$. Prove that
$$\frac1{1+a^3+b^3}+\frac1{1+b^3+c^3}+\frac1{1+c^3+a^3}\le1.$$

Cynthia laid down 7 rocks in a row where the leftmost and rightmost rocks are coloured White. She wants to give each of the 5 central rocks one of the colours: Red, Green, Blue or White so that
• to the right of any Red rock is either Green or White rock
• to the right of any Green rock is either Blue or White rock
• to the right of any Blue rock is either Red or White rock, and
• White rocks are never next to each other.
In how many ways can Cynthia colour the rocks?

In a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$, call $\alpha$ and $\beta$, the circumcircles of $ABC$ and $ACD$ respectively. Pick a point $E$ on $\alpha$ and line $EA$ passes through $\beta$ at $F$. Let $X$ be the intersection of $BE$ and $DF$. Prove that as the position of $E$ varies on $\alpha$, $X$ always stays on a fixed circle.

Let $p$ be an odd integer greater than $1$ such that $\gcd(p,3)=1$.
a) Prove that $p^6-1$ is divisible by $9$. (Hint: One can write $p=3k\pm1$ where $k$ is an integer. )
b) Prove that $p^6-1$ is divisible by $72$.
Suppose $a$ and $b$ are real numbers with $b\ne0$. Can both quadratics $x^2+ax+b^2=0$ and $x^2+bx+a^2=0$ have real roots simultaneously? Justify your answer.
Maung Kan Kaung rolls a fair die 7 times. What is the probability that he will roll each possible outcome $1,2,3,\dots,6$ at least once?

Let $ABC$ be a right triangle with $\angle A=90^\circ$, and $AB<AC$. Let $I$ be the incenter of $\triangle ABC$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of side $BC$. If $AI=IM$, show that $ABC$ is a $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$ right triangle.
Suppose that $a$, $b$ and $c$ are positive integers such that $2^a+2^b=2^c$. Find the remainder when $a+b+c$ is divided by $3$.

(a) Factorize the expression $xy+yz+zx+z^2$.
(b) For any positive real numbers $a,b,c$ such that $a+b+c=1$, show that
$$\frac1{ab+c}+\frac1{bc+a}+\frac1{ca+b}=\frac2{(a+b)(b+c)(c+a)}.$$
In how many ways can 6 boys and 6 girls to stand in a row so that every girl has an even number (possibly 0) of boys to her left?

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB<AC$ and circumcenter $O$, and let $D$ be the point on side $BC$ such that $AD\perp BC$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be points on line $AD$ such that $BX=AX$ and $CY=AY$. Lines $BX$ and $CY$ meet at $T$.
(a) Show that $T$ lies on the circumcircle of $\triangle BOC$.
(b) Show that $\angle AOT=90^\circ$.
If $x$ is an integer such that $3x^2+10x-8$ is divisible by $7$, prove that $3x^2+10x-8$ is divisible by $49$.

Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that the relation
$$(x-y)f(x+y)=xf(x)-f(y)^2$$
holds for all real numbers $x,y$.
(Remark: $f(x)=g(x)$ or $h(x)$ for all $x$ does not necessarily imply that $f(x)=g(x)$ for all $x$ or $f(x)=h(x)$ for all $x$.)

Island Logitopia has 1000 people consisting of Knights, Knaves and Clowns. Knights only say the truth, Knaves only say the lie and Clowns say random. One day, all Logitopians stood around a large circle and said the following two sentences: “Standing immediately to my left is not a Knight.” “I am standing between a Clown and a someone who is not a Clown.”
Find the maximum possible number of Knaves.

Let $O$ be the circumcenter of $\triangle ABC$ ($BC>AC>AB$) with the property $\angle C=3(\angle A-\angle B)$. Let $F$ be a point inside $\triangle ABC$ such that $\triangle BOC\sim\triangle CFA$. $AF$ meets $BC$ at $D$. Let $E$ be the reflection of $B$ over $D$.
(a) Show that $\triangle ABE$ is a right triangle.
(b) Prove that $AC$ bisects $\angle DAE$.

Suppose $a$ and $b$ are positive integers such that
$$a=\frac{b^2}{2!}+\frac{b^3}{3!}\quad\text{and}\quad b<2025.$$
Find the number of possible values of $a$.
